clue.text: He has a standoffish colleague needing, say, a couple of drinks

parts.note: SC is short for scilicet, Latin for 'that is to say' or 'namely'
a tot of rum is one drink and a half (half-pint of beer) is the other
a tot of rum is one drink and a half (half-pint of beer) is the other

explanation.surface: Someone aloof at work apparently needs a stiff drink or two to cope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standoffish' hides the rugby stand-off half (fly-half), who plays alongside this partner at half-back. SC is the old abbreviation of Latin scilicet, 'namely'.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union the stand-off and this player form the half-back pairing, so each is the other's closest teammate.

clue.text: It gives one the right angle in tennis games to get even

definitions.text: It gives one the right angle

parts.note: a set is a group of games in tennis
to square up is to settle or get even

explanation.surface: Advice on finding the right angle in tennis to level the score.
explanation.definitionFit: This triangular drawing instrument is used to draw lines at 90 degrees.

clue.text: Get up a Midlands waterway

parts.note: R is river, and the Ouse (Great Ouse) rises in the East Midlands
R is river, and the Ouse (Great Ouse) rises in the East Midlands

explanation.surface: A boat trip upstream on a canal in central England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' looks like a direction for travel, but 'Get up' is the definition; 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse is to wake someone or stir them from sleep.

clue.text: Building party using inadequate materials?

parts.note: making is building or constructing
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A construction gang working with poor supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means managing with whatever poor resources are to hand.

clue.text: Dislike a translation

parts.note: a version is a rendering or translation of a text

explanation.surface: Someone hates a rendering of a text.
explanation.definitionFit: Aversion means strong distaste or antipathy.

clue.text: Travel costs, including round the islands

indicators.note: the word for travel costs holds the round letter inside it

parts.note: fares are the charges for travel
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Ticket prices include a circular tour of the islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Faroes are a North Atlantic archipelago belonging to Denmark.

clue.text: Home brew-elicits two expressions of surprise

parts.note: ho and och are both exclamations of surprise, the second Scottish
ho and och are both exclamations of surprise, the second Scottish

explanation.surface: A homemade drink draws a couple of startled gasps from those tasting it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooch is slang for illicitly distilled or homemade liquor.

clue.text: Respect Jack, say

explanation.surface: Showing esteem for a man called Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a name; it is the playing card, one of the honours in bridge (ace, king, queen, jack, ten).
explanation.definitionFit: Honour means esteem or regard; in bridge the top cards of a suit are called honours.

clue.text: Exercise in speech for theatre job

indicators.note: the exercise letters go inside the word for a speech

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A drill in public speaking intended for a stage performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' looks like the stage, but it is an operating theatre in a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgery carried out in an operating theatre is a surgeon's procedure.

clue.text: Marriage in this state entails an act of contrition

definitions.text: Marriage in this state entails an act of contrition

parts.words: Marriage in this state entails an act of contrition
parts.note: alludes to the proverb that those who marry in a rush repent at leisure

explanation.surface: Getting married in a certain condition leads to remorse.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'marry in haste, repent at leisure' warns against rushed weddings.

clue.text: Give way in bed

explanation.surface: Someone yields while lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: To truckle is to submit meekly; a truckle bed is a low bed on castors stored under another.

clue.text: Field of beans

explanation.definitionFit: The field in a race is all its competitors, the starters; runner beans are a climbing bean grown in British gardens.

clue.text: Mill was unusual, having no middle name

indicators.note: the central letter of the five-letter word for unusual is dropped

parts.note: queer in its older sense means odd or unusual

explanation.surface: A mill was odd in having no central name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having no middle' removes the central E of QUEER, leaving QUER; 'was' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A quern is a small hand mill for grinding grain between two stones.

clue.text: Just think —- you'll be better to do this

definitions.text: you'll be better to do this

explanation.surface: Advice to ponder, as thinking will improve you.
explanation.definitionFit: To speculate is to ponder or conjecture; it is also to gamble on markets, which is what a better (one who bets) does.

clue.text: Sucker's sharp fall

parts.note: acid describes a sharp, sour taste
a drop is a fall

explanation.surface: A gullible person's steep descent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sucker' suggests a dupe, but it means a sweet that is sucked; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: This boiled sweet, sour-tasting, is a classic British confection for sucking.

clue.text: Award for excellence in german

parts.note: reads like a school prize for the language, but means a military decoration from Germany

explanation.surface: A school prize for top marks in German.
explanation.definitionFit: This medal was Prussia's and later Germany's decoration for military bravery.

clue.text: Do a farmer's job —- there may be money in it

definitions.text: there may be money in it

explanation.surface: A farm chore, and a hint that cash lies in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To till is to plough and cultivate land; a till is a cash register drawer in a shop.

clue.text: It's hateful at home, so student moves

parts.note: L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

indicators.note: the letters of the three words shift around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A student moving out of a home that is miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hateful' is the definition and 'It's' a link; L for learner is the usual shorthand for a student.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathsome means detestable, causing loathing or disgust.

clue.text: Enticing little swimmers may be a bit evil

indicators.note: says the letters might become something else when rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Luring small fish could be slightly wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Small fish kept alive on a hook to lure bigger fish are used by anglers as bait.

clue.text: Shiny silver paper left about

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
litter is rubbish such as paper left lying around

explanation.surface: Silver paper scattered around gleams.
explanation.definitionFit: Aglitter means glittering or sparkling.

clue.text: A little grey otter in river island

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A small grey otter lives on an island in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'in', but 'in' is the link joining wordplay and definition; the definition is 'river island'.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyot (or ait) is a small island in a river, especially the Thames.

clue.text: West Indian group has a supplier of smokes

parts.note: the Virgin Islands are a Caribbean group, with I standing for Islands as in map abbreviations
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Caribbean band turns out to have a tobacco connection.
explanation.walkthrough: The Virgin Islands are shortened to VIRGIN I, I being the usual abbreviation for island; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia is a type of tobacco named after the American state that grew it, so it supplies cigarettes.

clue.text: Make one's way round boundary in very proper fashion

indicators.note: the word for making one's way goes around the boundary word

parts.note: to ply is to travel a route regularly
a rim is an edge or boundary

explanation.surface: Walking politely around the edge of a field.
explanation.definitionFit: Primly means in a stiffly correct, prudish way.

clue.text: Fan's call for prompt victory

parts.note: a win is a victory
now means immediately, promptly

explanation.surface: A supporter's cry urging the team to win quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' looks like a supporter, matching the call to win, but means to blow air through grain; 'call for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To winnow is to blow the chaff from grain with a current of air, as a fan does.

clue.text: Attacking in writing

parts.note: taken as written
cursive is joined-up handwriting

explanation.surface: Being aggressive on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: An incursive force is one making raids or incursions, hence aggressive.

clue.text: Presume one sounds warmly dressed

indicators.note: the phrase is heard as spoken rather than as spelt

parts.note: someone in fur is warmly clad

explanation.surface: Assume that someone is heard to be well wrapped up.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to deduce or conclude from evidence.

clue.text: Sort of bull from John Bull's other island?

explanation.surface: A bull hailing from another British island.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish bull is a ludicrous self-contradictory statement; Shaw's play John Bull's Other Island is about Ireland, John Bull being England personified.

clue.text: Early Christian settlement. I held, was once in Asia Minor

indicators.note: the settlement holds the single letter within it

parts.note: Iona is the Scottish island where St Columba founded a monastery in 563

explanation.surface: An early monastery says it once stood in what is now Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: IONA is a small island off western Scotland, a cradle of Celtic Christianity.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionia was an ancient Greek coastal region of western Anatolia, no longer existing.

clue.text: Servant is a base fellow

parts.note: the foot of something is its base
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A servant is called a low and contemptible chap.
explanation.definitionFit: A footman is a liveried male household attendant.

clue.text: Vivaldi's Merchant of Venice?

explanation.surface: The Baroque composer is linked to Shakespeare's Venetian trader.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio was Vivaldi's first name; Antonio is also the title merchant who borrows from Shylock in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Weedy, so nervous of football?

explanation.surface: A feeble person who is scared of a ball game.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading treats the word as rush-shy, wary of a rush (a forward charge with the ball in football); 'so' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rushy means overgrown with rushes, a kind of waterside weed; the second sense is a punning coinage.

clue.text: Conspiracy that may deny access to river

definitions.text: that may deny access to river

explanation.surface: A plot connected with something blocking the way to a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Watergate was the 1970s Nixon political scandal and cover-up; a water gate is a gate controlling access to or flow of a waterway.
